White, near white or white blend Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: MEImagarmic
Exhibition name: Princesse de Monaco ®
rows.Origin:
Bred by Marie-Louise (Louisette) Meilland (Paolino) (1920-1987) (France, 1971).
Introduced in France by Meilland et Cie in 1981 as 'Princesse de Monaco'.
Introduced in Australia by Ross Roses in 1985 as 'Princesse de Monaco'.
rows.Bloom: Cream, pink edges. Mild, fruity fragrance. 35 to 45 petals. Average diameter 4.75". Very large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, cupped bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Large, wide oval buds.
rows.Habit:
Short, bushy, upright. Large, glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 28" to 3' (70 to 90cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower or garden. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .

rows.Notes: In September 1998, the Montreal Botanical Garden (Le Jardin Botanique de Montreal) carried out a survey of its roses' resistance to black spot, powdery mildew and rust. This is one of the outstanding varieties which showed a 0% to 5% infection rate. The data were taken on well-established roses.
